metadata.dcterms:title: Sum rule for the Compton amplitude and implications for the proton-neutron mass difference
metadata.dcterms:creator: Gasser1, J.
Leutwyler1, H.
Rusetsky2, A.
metadata.dcterms:abstract: The Cottingham formula expresses the lead- ing contribution of the electromagnetic interaction to the proton-neutron mass diﬀerence as an integral over the forward Compton amplitude. Since quarks and glu- ons reggeize, the dispersive representation of this ampli- tude requires a subtraction. We assume that the asymp- totic behaviour is dominated by Reggeon exchange. This leads to a sum rule that expresses the subtraction function in terms of measurable quantities. The evalua- tion of this sum rule leads to mp−n QED = 0.58 ± 0.16 MeV.
